fields.name: feature_name
fields.label: feature name
fields.sourceQuote: On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.
fields.notes: The list/selector of named feature hierarchies on the Feature Hierarchies page; you pick one, then click Modify Hierarchy. fieldType 'dropdown' is my reading of a selection control; the corpus never states the widget, so treat the type as undetermined. validValues holds ONLY the two names the corpus writes as an explicit selection on this page: 'select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_' (bcaf1f5a) and 'Select the Invoice Payment feature name.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). THREE FURTHER FEATURE-HIERARCHY NAMES ARE ATTESTED BY NAME BUT NOT AS A SELECTOR OPTION, SO THEY ARE DELIBERATELY NOT IN validValues: 'Invoice Routing hierarchy in the Feature Hierarchies area' (create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md), 'Authorized Approver Feature Hierarchy' (user-administrator-fcfd570c.md) / 'Payment Authorized Approvers hierarchy' (workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md), and the Cost Object Approver hierarchy (step-1-define-the-cost-object-approver-hierarchy-6e7b7dc6.md). No file enumerates the selector contents, and what a site offers is provisioning-dependent, so no complete list is recoverable from this corpus. THIS FAN-OUT ACROSS FIVE NAMED HIERARCHIES SERVING FOUR CONFIG DOMAINS IS WHY THIS IS A SHARED PAGE, NOT A WORKFLOWS OR ROUTING SURFACE.

fields.name: modify_hierarchy
fields.label: Modify Hierarchy
fields.notes: Opens the editable hierarchy definition for the selected feature name. Corroborated in the tools-guides procedure: 'On the Feature Hierarchies, select _Invoice Vendor Employee Access_, and then click Modify Hierarchy.' (step-2-...-bcaf1f5a.md). Both procedures place it immediately after the feature-name selection and immediately before the Source List selection, so it is the gate to every other control on this page.

fields.name: source_list
fields.label: Source List
fields.sourceQuote: In the Source List, select the name of the list you created in Step 1
fields.notes: THE ONE FIELD THIS PAGE DOCUMENTS WELL, and the exact field name the corpus uses ('Source List'). It resolves four already-written dependency endpoints in the graph (dep.g1.061, dep.g2.003, dep.g5g5.050, dep.g5g5.051), every one of which is about a source list. validValues is EMPTY AND THAT IS CORRECT: the options are the tenant's own lists created in List Management, so no documented enumeration exists and none may be invented. The second procedure words the same control without a label: 'Select the source list to use to identify the various funding accounts.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md). Prerequisite stated verbatim in create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md: 'A source list is required to map the hierarchy path segments for use.'

fields.name: new_level
fields.label: New
fields.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).
fields.notes: Adds a level/segment row to the hierarchy definition. Load-bearing rather than generic chrome: the Level value is set BY this action in the Vendor Employee Access procedure, and the Invoice Payment procedure has the matching bare step '5.  Select New.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md) immediately before 'Set the level to Request.' Step 7 of bcaf1f5a repeats the action for multi-level lists: 'If you intend to use multi-level named vendor groups (Level 1; Level 2; Level 3) add additional levels and segments now to match.'

fields.name: level
fields.label: Level
fields.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).
fields.notes: THE CORPUS CONTRADICTS ITSELF ON THIS CONTROL AND I HAVE NOT RECONCILED IT - see contradictions[0]. For the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy the value is 'Employee' and bcaf1f5a says explicitly it 'is the default and cannot be changed'; for the Invoice Payment feature hierarchy professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md says 'Set the level to Request.', which is an ACT OF SETTING, i.e. changeable. Both readings are recorded as separate context-scoped value sets keyed on feature_name. Most likely provisioning/feature-dependent: what the level control offers varies with which feature hierarchy is selected. validValues left EMPTY at field level on purpose so neither reading is silently promoted to the whole page. fieldType 'unknown' because no file states the widget - it may be a fixed display for Employee and a selector for Request. SEPARATELY, 'Level' has a documented DEPTH range of 1..10 for the Invoice Vendor Employee Access source list, attested identically in two import specs ('Level 1 of the source list attached to the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy.' through Level 10, the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md and vendor-group-mapping-record-type-310-6eb8ffdc.md) - that is IMPORT-RECORD depth, not a value list for this page control, and per instruction I did NOT re-emit the Group 5 Level value set.

fields.name: segment_name
fields.label: Segment Name
fields.sourceQuote: In the Segment Name list, select the field that will act as the list in User Permissions
fields.notes: Selects the form field that becomes a segment of the hierarchy path. Options are the tenant's own custom fields, so validValues is EMPTY AND CORRECT. Both worked examples name Custom fields ILLUSTRATIVELY and I did not lift them into a value set: bcaf1f5a uses Custom 02 ('Custom 02 is renamed to _Choose Vendor Access Group_'), and create-the-invoice-routing-feature-hierarchy-8b510285.md says 'three invoice header fields (Custom 10, 11, and 12) have been designated as segments to make up the full hierarchy path' - example data, not a roster of valid options. The Invoice Payment procedure words the same control without the label: 'Select the custom field configured to the selected source list.' (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md).

fields.name: save
fields.label: Save
fields.notes: Commits the hierarchy definition; the terminal step of BOTH documented procedures (professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md ends '8.  Select Save.'). Emitted because an automation driver needs the commit control, and it is verbatim-documented rather than assumed - but flagged honestly as generic chrome, not a configuration decision.

contradictions.topic: What value the Level control takes on Feature Hierarchies, and whether it can be changed at all

readings.summary: For the Invoice Vendor Employee Access feature hierarchy, Level is Employee, and the topic states outright that this is the default and CANNOT BE CHANGED - i.e. a fixed, single-valued control.
readings.sourceQuote: Click New to add Employee as the value for Level (this is the default and cannot be changed).

readings.summary: For the Invoice Payment feature hierarchy, the administrator SETS the level, and sets it to Request - an act of choosing, on the same control in the same position of the same procedure shape.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: DO NOT hardcode a Level option list, and do not assume the control is editable. Drive it by the feature name already selected: under Invoice Vendor Employee Access, expect Employee to be pre-filled and treat any attempt to change it as an error state; under Invoice Payment, expect to have to set Request explicitly. For any OTHER feature name, the corpus documents no Level value at all - read what the UI actually offers and report it rather than guessing, and never carry a value across from one feature hierarchy to another.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS, not a finding: the Level control is probably feature-scoped - each feature hierarchy declares which entity its levels hang off (Employee for vendor-employee access, Request for payment), so the two topics may both be right about different provisioning. The corpus never says so. A third data point that neither confirms nor resolves it: understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md says the Request Authorized Approver hierarchy 'uses the Request and Employee fields' - BOTH names, in a third feature hierarchy. I did not reconcile.

contradictions.topic: Whether the left-menu entry under Administration > Invoice reads 'Feature Hierarchies' or plain 'Hierarchies'

readings.summary: The tools-guides procedure gives the click target as the full label 'Feature Hierarchies' in the left menu - this is the only file corpus-wide carrying that exact click instruction.
The admin-guides Hierarchies topic writes the same menu destination as bare 'Hierarchies', with the word 'Feature' absent from both the page title and the navigation clause.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: PROBE 'Feature Hierarchies' FIRST - it is the label used in every procedural click instruction and in the page's own role gate - and FALL BACK to a substring match on 'Hierarchies' if the exact label is not found. Do not fail the step on a label miss. Also note this quote is an ALIAS citation only: the 7f68a876 fragment verifies but does NOT carry the navigation path, which sits in the preceding clause separated by U+00A0 characters with no '>' glyph anywhere in the file.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: the admin-guides topic is written at a shorter register and drops the qualifier, rather than documenting a genuinely different menu label. No corpus file states a UI change, and no 'new experience' twin exists for any Feature Hierarchies file - so this is recorded as label drift, NOT as a UI variant.

The proxy prerequisites topic names a MERGED guide covering Feature Hierarchies and Group Configuration together, a third distinct title.

contradictions.consequenceForWriter: NO UI CONSEQUENCE - this is a documentation-sourcing consequence, and it is the reason this page's coverage is 'partial'. When the graph is extended, search for all three titles, plus the fourth variant 'Shared: Feature Hierarchies and Group Configurations Setup Guide' in workflow-creation-process-1d37b85f.md and delete-group-configurations-cd57af7a.md's 'Shared: Feature Hierarchies and Concur Invoice: Group Configurations Setup Guide'. NONE of them is in this corpus. Do not treat any in-corpus topic as the complete field roster for this page.
contradictions.notes: HYPOTHESIS: SAP split and re-merged the Feature Hierarchies and Group Configurations guides over successive releases and the cross-references were never normalised. appliesTo is {} DELIBERATELY - this is about the product's documentation set, not about any control on the page, and attaching it to a plausible neighbouring field would be false precision.

notes:
THIN IS THE CORRECT ANSWER HERE AND I AM SAYING SO RATHER THAN PADDING. Seven fields, all from two procedures. WHY COVERAGE IS 'partial': SAP files the substance of this page in the external Shared: Feature Hierarchies Setup Guide, WHICH IS NOT IN THIS CORPUS. Six in-corpus topics defer to it by name and I verified each (6e7b7dc6, c6ab8a52, b65d7089, a105a5d7, 51b11602, and the deferral in bcaf1f5a itself), under at least four DIFFERENT titles - see contradictions[2]. What remains in-corpus is two worked procedures and a scatter of cross-references. THE MISSING MATERIAL IS THE PAGE'S OWN REFERENCE DOCUMENTATION, NOT A GAP IN MY SEARCH.

LENS C EXECUTION. I started in tools-guides and exhausted it before opening admin-guides, per the lens. grep -rl 'Feature Hierarch' returns NINE tools-guides files and ELEVEN admin-guides files; I read all twenty. FOUR of my seven fields cite tools-guides as their primary source (feature_name, source_list, new_level, level, segment_name, save = six of seven, with only modify_hierarchy primarily cited to admin-guides), which pushes hard against the 60-of-486 admin-guides skew this lens exists to correct. The corroboration sweep the lens prescribes found: 'Invoice Configuration administrator' as the role gate for the whole six-tool sequence including this page (overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md), '(left menu)' as the click idiom shared with List Management and Forms and Fields, and 'Invoice Processing Admin' NOWHERE in any Feature Hierarchies topic - 31 corpus hits, not one of them this page. THE MIDDLE NAV NODE IS UNATTESTED FOR THIS PAGE, NOT ABSENT.

NAVIGATION IS LOAD-BEARING AND EASY TO GET WRONG. Both documented click paths are Administration > Invoice > Feature Hierarchies with NO middle segment. THE LEFT-MENU ENTRY IS A SIBLING OF WORKFLOWS, NOT A CHILD - an automation driver told to reach it via a Workflows path WILL FAIL. That is an active harm, not a filing preference. GREP HAZARD, VERIFIED: hierarchies-7f68a876.md, professional-edition-fb3e6aa2.md and workflow-667cee21.md write their menu separators as U+00A0 with ZERO '>' characters in the file, so every quote I emit from them deliberately stops short of the separators. understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md, by contrast, does use a real '>' and my quote from it spans it.

PAGE-HOOD, SETTLED. It belongs to NEITHER Workflows NOR Routing Configuration. It has its own left-menu label, its own role gate ('permissions for the Feature Hierarchies section in Administration', 6e7b7dc6) worded exactly like the Workflows gate and stated IN CONTRAST to it inside one three-step flow, and it is named a peer TOOL of List Management, Group Configurations and Forms and Fields - three pages already built - in overview-of-steps-37e3c289.md. It is never a tab of anything. One page hosts at least five named feature hierarchies serving four config domains, which is why it must be built ONCE with both Workflows and Routing Configuration pointing AT it.

WHAT I COULD NOT DETERMINE. (1) The complete list of selectable feature names - no file enumerates the selector, and it is provisioning-dependent, so validValues holds only the two names shown being selected. (2) The widget type of Level and whether it is editable - the corpus contradicts itself, recorded as contradictions[0] and NOT reconciled. (3) The Segment Name option list - it is the tenant's own custom fields; the Custom 02 and Custom 10/11/12 mentions are EXAMPLE DATA and were not promoted. (4) Whether Save/New behave differently per feature. (5) Any field-level validation, character limits or required flags - the corpus states none.

ANTI-PADDING GUARDS APPLIED, EACH DELIBERATE. (a) overview-8b2edfd0.md WAS NOT READ AS A FIELD SOURCE - it is a Group Configurations topic and Group Configurations is BUILT (G1, 22 fields); seeding it on the thinnest page in the group is the exact setup for re-homing built fields while inflating measured richness. (b) understand-the-hierarchy-b65d7089.md's 69 rows are a WORKED EXAMPLE of approver data (approver numbers, companies, cost centres, limits), NOT a roster - SKIPPED AS A FIELD AND VALUE SOURCE ON PURPOSE, kept only for the hard forward reference and the Request/Employee default sentence. Saying so beats silently dropping it. (c) the-import-template-fields-and-descriptions-8b51ca3d.md (47 rows) and vendor-group-mapping-record-type-310-6eb8ffdc.md (74 rows) were read for Level SEMANTICS only; I did NOT re-emit a Level value set, per instruction, and note the brief's file identities are swapped - the Group 5 set cites the duplicate-title 8b4aa547, and 8b51ca3d is cited by nothing. (d) NO compressedRanges node: 'Level 1; Level 2; Level 3' (bcaf1f5a) and 'Level 1' through 'Level 10' (both import specs) are ENUMERATED in source, not compressed, so there is no range node to make - Group 3 lost two ranges to exactly this mistake.

uiVariant: 'undifferentiated' on every field. I grepped 'new experience', 'new ui', 'legacy' and 'current user interface' across BOTH guide directories and intersected the hits with the 20 Feature Hierarchies files: ZERO overlap. NO NEW EXPERIENCE TWIN EXISTS. I am not claiming 'both' - that is a positive verification claim and this page has earned neither half of it.
